newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: AVI SAYS IN MORE OVERSEAS TIE-UP TALKS.
newsitem.headline: AVI SAYS IN MORE OVERSEAS TIE-UP TALKS.

text.p: South Africa's Anglovaal Industries Ltd (AVI) said on Monday that an earlier announced deal with U.S. tyre giant Goodyear Tire and Rubber Co could be followed by more overseas tie-ups.
AVI managing director Richard Savage said on Monday that the firm was already in a number of separate talks.
"We are in discussions with other international companies where we have had relationships over a broad spectrum," he told a news conference.
Savage said that the negotiations meant that shareholders in AVI and Anglovaal should continue to exercise caution when dealing in the companies' stock until further announcements were made.

Earlier Goodyear said it was returning to South Africa after disinvesting in the 1980s, acquiring 60 percent of tyre and engineered products concern Contred (Pty) Ltd from AVI for 437 million rand in cash. Including assumed debt, the purchase price rises to 568 million rand.
AVI will control the remaining 40 percent of Contred.
Goodyear chief executive and president Samir Gibara said the partnership would launch an export drive into neighbouring countries using South Africa as a base for the rest of the continent.
The drive would especially focus on opportunities in the mining industry, he said.

"We will grow our business, provide exports to sub-Saharan and other African countries, develop state-of-the-art products, especially for applications in the many mining operations on the continent," Gibara said.
Savage also said the African market would be an area of expansion. "We see tremendous opportunities in developing these markets in conjunction with Goodyear," he said.
Savage said the talks that led to the Goodyear deal had taken 12 months to complete. AVI had entered the discussions in order to compete in a world market where trade barriers are coming down.
"Our businesses in South Africa have to become internationally competitive," he said.

Savage said this need for international expertise and access to world markets was the reason why AVI was prepared to take a minority stake in Contred -- breaking its usual policy of insisting on at least 51 percent of any venture.
